card.occupation: Self-employed upholsterer, working about 12 to 14 hours a week from a rented unit on a small trading estate, mostly reupholstering dining chairs, footstools and the odd armchair for local customers
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Abingdon, then a BTEC in Art and Design at college. Did retail and admin work through her twenties, then took a part-time City & Guilds upholstery course in her early thirties and set up on her own after an informal apprenticeship with an older upholsterer who has since retired
card.household: Lives in a three-bed 1990s semi with her husband Rob (39, an electrician for a facilities firm) and their daughter Isla (8). A rescue greyhound called Pip mostly lives on the sofa
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in South Oxfordshire. Her parents still live in Abingdon. Church of England: she was christened and confirmed and got married in church. Now she goes mainly at Christmas, Easter and for Isla's school services, but she does think of herself as Christian and says a quiet prayer now and then
card.professional_persona: Careful, patient and quietly proud of her work. She likes the detective part of a job, stripping back old chairs and finding horsehair stuffing or someone's 1970s repair underneath. She is honest with customers about what's worth doing and what isn't. She tends to undercharge, which Rob teases her about. Most of her work comes through word of mouth and a small Instagram page
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She walks Pip most mornings around Ladygrove and the lakes, and she did a Couch to 5K a couple of years ago and still goes to the local parkrun every so often. She'll watch the Six Nations with Rob but doesn't follow it closely
card.arts_persona: Very visual and drawn to textiles, pattern and colour. She follows fabric designers online, loves William Morris prints and has been to the V&A twice for textile exhibitions. She sketches ideas in a cheap notebook and reads a fair bit of fiction, mostly book-club picks and historical novels. She'd like to try screen printing one day
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK holidays: Cornwall, the Norfolk coast, a cottage in Wales with Rob's family. They went to Crete before Isla was born and keep meaning to go abroad again. She loves wandering round a new town's charity shops and antique centres and will happily lose an afternoon in one
card.culinary_persona: A decent everyday cook, nothing fancy. Pasta bakes, curries from a jar with extra veg, a roast on Sundays if they're not at her mum's. Calls the evening meal dinner. She enjoys trying recipes she's seen online and bakes with Isla at weekends, with mixed results
hobbies_and_interests: Charity shop and car boot hunting for old furniture
Monthly book club with friends from Isla's school
Watching Great British Sewing Bee and property shows
skills: Sewing machine work, including piping and cushions
Estimating jobs and dealing with customers
Running a small Instagram page for the business
card.career_goals: To build the business up slowly to three or four days a week once Isla is older, and maybe run small weekend workshops teaching people to do their own drop-in seats. She'd also like to make some pieces of her own to sell rather than only doing commissions
card.voice: Friendly, fairly middle-of-the-road southern English accent, neither posh nor strongly local. Moderate pace, speeding up a little when she's talking about something she enjoys. Uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' and 'kind of' as soft hedges, and finishes points with 'you know' or 'yeah'. Says 'sorry' to repair a sentence ('it was, sorry, it was the second one'). Picks up the other person's words when engaged. She'll fill a short silence with a little laugh or 'erm, what else', but she's comfortable pausing to think if she's asked something properly
card.typing: Mostly lowercase in quick answers, with a capital for names sometimes. Uses commas rather than full stops and keeps apostrophes most of the time but not always ('dont'). Occasional 'tbh' or 'lol', the odd typo she doesn't fix, and sometimes an exclamation mark if she's being friendly
card.with_strangers: Warm, easy and a bit self-deprecating. She asks questions back and is quick to agree or find common ground. She can be slightly reticent about money or opinions she thinks might cause friction, but she's genuinely curious and opens up once the conversation gets going
small_things: Pip refusing to walk in the rain
a lovely bit of velvet she found at a car boot
Isla's school play or reading book
being knackered after a long stapling session
a book club book nobody finished
a customer's chair with dog hair in the stuffing
deeper_things: She sometimes feels she 'gave up' on art after college and only found her way back through upholstery
She worries the business isn't 'a proper job' to some people, including her dad
They tried for a second child for a few years, and she has made a kind of peace with it being just Isla
Her faith is quieter than it used to be, but she finds church comforting when things are hard
Money is fine but tight some months, and she feels guilty about how little the business brings in
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, so the frame looks up a little. Head and shoulders, slightly off-centre to the left. Daylight comes from a window off to her right, lighting that side of her face more brightly. She has a friendly, open face with a few freckles and minimal makeup, and a half-smile as if mid-sentence. Shoulder-length mid-brown hair is pulled back loosely in a clip, with a few strands loose. No glasses. She wears a dark green crew-neck jumper with the sleeves pushed up. Behind her is a kitchen-diner wall painted pale grey, with a wooden shelf holding cookbooks, a small potted plant and a jar of pens. A corkboard is pinned with a school letter and a couple of fabric swatches. The edge of a fridge with a child's drawing stuck on it shows at the right of the frame
